parsed.explanation: Documented routine police harassment, extortion and detention of trans people, custody abuse with nonconsensual medical procedures in 2025, and an upheld same-sex criminalisation regime used as a police lever keep consequences after outing severe, including imprisonment. Courts have provided real relief against forced examinations and for association and resident markers, and the death-penalty bill is not law, but no implementing protection is recorded and police abuse persists. Entry handling is undocumented, so no safety credit is taken from silence.

entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; resident marker refusal and the 2026 resident-marker ruling do not document border acceptance. Interaction status uncertain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented routine detention on pretexts, detention beyond constitutional period without charges, extortion, rape by security officers, and 2025 incarceration with nonconsensual medical procedures and court-ordered gender determination.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2025 High Court found dignity, privacy and freedom-from-torture violations in custody and directed protective legislation; no enacted response recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police cell-placement difficulty and custody abuse show outed detainees may be placed and examined by assigned sex, compounding detention exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Trans people fear sex-designated bathrooms fearing accusation of sexual crimes; police difficulty deciding male or female cells when detained.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Prisons were found to fail dignity and privacy protections in 2025, but no operative facility-access protection for visitors is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility and custody uncertainty interacts with police stops: being read as gender-nonconforming can trigger both public-space and custody exposure.

care_services.exposure: Documented barriers to gender-affirming care, including a 2012 refusal of surgery without reasons at a national referral hospital; current visitor access not documented.
care_services.interaction: Care denial is dated and resident-focused; for a visitor it is a secondary signal of institutional non-recognition rather than a proven border or clinic rule.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Sections 162 and 165 criminalise same-sex acts up to 14 and 5 years; 2019 High Court upheld them, appeal decision not recorded. Police use related pretexts for harassment and extortion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Forced anal examinations ruled unconstitutional in 2018 with compensation in 2024; 2023 Supreme Court upheld association. Family Protection Bill proposing death is stalled, not law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Same-sex law is secondary for trans visitors but documented as a police lever against gender-nonconforming people, interacting with detention and extortion.

minors_guardians.interaction: No visitor-specific rule for minors or guardians is documented; resident adoption ineligibility does not establish a traveller exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Widespread societal discrimination and anti-LGBTQ sentiment documented; a resident was killed in 2024 and the assailant received 50 years. No trans-specific or general rates are provided, so magnitude is unstated.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Prosecution and 50-year sentence in the 2024 killing, plus court remedies noted above, show some state response, contrasted with documented rape and extortion by security officers.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Purposive 2025 documentation describes reported cases, not prevalence; violence exposure cannot be quantified but police-perpetrated abuse is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No explicit statutory SOGI anti-discrimination protection; no enacted Transgender Protection Rights Act recorded; criminalisation appeal outcome unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional claims have succeeded in court, including 2018, 2023, 2025 and 2026 rulings, and human-rights commission documentation exists, though civic space is described as restrictive.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court relief is real but implementation is undocumented; entry, border and visitor-specific remedies remain unknown and are not treated as protections.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: repeated police extortion, document confiscation and overnight detention with weak oversight. This case is similar or slightly higher because courts have granted documented relief and compensation, but custody abuse and a 14-year statute keep it in this tier.

Lower: 0.35-B involves hours-long stops and fines rarely becoming imprisonment. Here detention beyond the constitutional period, sexual violence by security, 2025 custodial medical abuse and an upheld imprisonment statute make severity materially higher.

Much lower: 0.65-A has national equality protection, no detention for mismatch and reliable court-ordered release. Here trans-specific protection is absent in statute, criminalisation remains upheld, and police harassment is documented as routine.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is hostile in first contact: outed visitors face documented police stops, extortion, pretext detention and possible custody abuse, within a criminalisation regime that police have used to target gender-nonconforming people. Courts are the strongest mitigating feature, having blocked forced examinations, upheld association and ordered resident marker reform, but their directives lack recorded implementing law and do not restrain documented street-level abuse. No execution regime is in force and one killing was heavily punished, preventing a lower score. Undocumented entry handling cannot offset these known exposures.
